title: Mamata Banerjee's camp sends truckloads of affidavits to Election Commission in Trinamool fight
dek: Her faction says it has sworn statements from 17 MPs and dozens of MLAs in its claim to the party's name and twin-flower symbol. The rival Ritabrata Banerjee camp says it filed twice as many documents.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Mamata Banerjee's faction of the Trinamool Congress delivered three truckloads of documents to the Election Commission of India in New Delhi on Sunday, including affidavits it says show that most of the party's MPs and founders back her claim to the Trinamool name and its twin-flower symbol, according to reports.

The rival Democratic Trinamool Congress, led by Ritabrata Banerjee, the Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly, has said it filed six truckloads of its own documents earlier this month. The Commission is expected to examine both sets of papers before it holds hearings, at which each side can challenge the other's claims.

## What was submitted

The trucks arrived at the Commission's office one after another on Sunday afternoon, with Trinamool MPs Kalyan Banerjee, Derek O'Brien and Dola Sen present, according to reports. One report said the documents had been kept at the residence of the party's general secretary, Abhishek Banerjee, before they were sent.

The faction says the bundle includes affidavits from 17 MPs (eight in the Lok Sabha and nine in the Rajya Sabha), from six of the party's seven surviving founding members, and from members of its national working committee. Reports differ on the number of legislators: one report said the affidavits came from 32 West Bengal MLAs elected on the twin-flower symbol, alongside legislators from Meghalaya and Assam, while another put the faction's claimed support at 38 MLAs.

Kalyan Banerjee said lakhs of party workers and supporters backed Mamata Banerjee. He questioned the authenticity of the rival camp's affidavits, alleged that some carried forged signatures, and said his side would share copies of its own documents with the other camp and its lawyers, reports said.

## What the other side says

Akhruzzaman, a leader of the Ritabrata Banerjee camp, said its affidavits carried the signatures of more than 12 lakh workers, leaders and supporters, according to reports. The faction filed its documents on 5 November, one report said. No response from the faction to the forgery allegation had been reported by Monday afternoon.

Union Minister of State Sukanta Majumdar of the BJP, which governs the state, dismissed Mamata Banerjee's faction as no longer a significant political force, reports said.

## Background

The Trinamool split after it lost the Assembly election in May to the BJP, ending its 15 years in power, and Suvendu Adhikari became chief minister. Pending a final decision on who owns the party's name and symbol, the Commission in September gave the two sides temporary identities, reports said: the Mamata Banerjee faction became the "Mamata All India Trinamool Congress" with a "Football Player" symbol, and the rebels the "Democratic Trinamool Congress" with an "Envelope" symbol.

In such disputes the Commission usually weighs support within a party's legislative and organisational wings, which is why both sides are collecting signed statements. Separately, the Mamata Banerjee faction has asked for 10 rebel MLAs, including Ritabrata Banerjee, to be disqualified under the anti-defection law; the Speaker has not ruled, and the Supreme Court this month sent that dispute to the Calcutta High Court.

Last week Abhishek Banerjee asked the Commission to protect documents prepared for the dispute after a security structure outside his Kolkata home was demolished, alleging that people linked to the BJP might try to take them. The police and the BJP have not responded to those allegations in detail.

## What happens next

The Commission has not announced a date for hearings. Its decision will determine which faction can contest future elections, including the Kolkata civic polls, under the Trinamool name and twin-flower symbol.
